subject: Operational continuity: recovery manifest & KPI snapshot
messages:
From: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@catalystfinance.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: Marcus Chen <marcus.chen@catalystfinance.com>, procure@catalystfinance.com
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Operational continuity — recovery manifest & KPI snapshot

Hi Markus,

Thanks for picking this up. As part of our SIG/CAIQ review and internal procurement checklist we need a concise recovery manifest for Redwood that covers: RTO and RPO commitments by workload class, heatmap of recovery responsibilities (Redwood vs customer), the last three DR test run summaries, and a CSV snapshot of your RTO/RPO KPIs over the past 12 months.

Specific asks:
- Canonical runbook or manifest that enumerates steps for cold, warm, and hot recovery for the hosted API and Dedicated pools.
- Measured time-to-restore for KV/warm-cache scenarios for serving runtime (we track warm cache as critical to latency SLAs).
- Evidence of the most recent full failover drill and replay logs.
- Mapping to SIG/CAIQ controls related to continuity and availability (if you can point to a short mapping table or section in the manifest).

Can you provide these assets by end of week? We may need to route a quick follow-up call with our infra team (Marcus and procure@) to confirm timelines.

Appreciate it — Hannah
Hannah Lee
Senior Security Programs Manager
Catalyst Finance

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@catalystfinance.com>
Cc: Marcus Chen <marcus.chen@catalystfinance.com>, rachel.kim@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Operational continuity — recovery manifest & KPI snapshot

Hannah — thanks for the clear list. High level: we can produce a single recovery manifest PDF that includes a controls mapping to SIG/CAIQ and a separate CSV with the KPI snapshots. I'm attaching the initial artifacts and a trace extract from our warm-cache warmup during the last rehearsal.

Attachments included: recovery-manifest-20261116.pdf (manifest + mapping), rto-rpo-kpi-snapshot.csv (12mo), warm-cache-warmup-trace.txt (sample trace), dr-test-202608-replay.log (most recent full failover replay).

Quick notes:
- RTO tiers: 1) Interactive API (p95 path) — target RTO 2 minutes for warm start, 15 minutes for full cold restore; 2) Batch/Background workloads — target RTO 60 minutes; 3) Dedicated Reserved Pools — SLA-backed 5 minutes for autoscale burst state (where configured).
- RPO: typical warm-cache-backed workloads have near-zero RPO (cache-backed checkpoints); for full system restore (cold) we publish up to 1 hour retention policy in our manifest but can lengthen via contractual commitments.
- The manifest includes an operations contact matrix and escalation steps.

If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough with our Reliability and Product Security teams later this week.

— Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Enterprise Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Chen <marcus.chen@catalystfinance.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@catalystfinance.com>, procure@catalystfinance.com
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Operational continuity — recovery manifest & KPI snapshot

Markus — thanks for the artifacts. A couple quick clarifying questions before we route to our infra SREs:

1) The manifest references warm-cache healing times (section 4.2) but the CSV has aggregate KPI buckets. Can you surface the worst-case warm-cache rebuild duration we observed in the last 12 months during a simulated region failover? We need to understand the tail.
2) For Dedicated Reserved Pools: does the 5-minute SLA assume pre-warmed model artifacts on local NVMe, or is that with model fetch from S3+quantization step?
3) Do you have signed change logs (immutable) from the last full failover rehearsal we can include for our compliance folder?

If you can answer inline and provide the worst-case trace and the signed change log, we should be able to close here.

— Marcus
Infra Ops Lead
Catalyst Finance

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Chen <marcus.chen@catalystfinance.com>, markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: rachel.kim@redwood.com, sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 11:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Operational continuity — recovery manifest & KPI snapshot

Marcus — copying the specific excerpts you requested. Quoting your questions below.

> 1) worst-case warm-cache rebuild duration during simulated region failover?

Observed worst-case: 82 seconds to reach functional KV-set rebuild for the p95 traffic profile during our Aug 2026 cross-region rehearsal (attached trace shows the timeline). Typical median rebuild for the same test was 18s; p95 is 48s, and worst tail spike 82s (affected by concurrent model warmup). Section 4.2 in the manifest documents mitigation steps (parallel KV fetch, prioritized hot-key warming) that reduced median rebuild by ~60% across subsequent canary runs.

> 2) Dedicated Reserved Pools SLA assumptions for 5-minute recovery?

That SLA is conditional: it assumes model artifacts are pre-pulled and quantized to the local node NVMe (our Dedicated onboarding process supports image prewarm and artifact pinning). If a customer opts out of pre-pulling, the measured recovery can be up to 20–30 minutes depending on model size and quantization stage. We call this out in the manifest under "Onboarding & Prewarm requirements."

> 3) signed change logs for last full failover rehearsal

We publish replay logs and an immutable rehearsal manifest signed by our SRE lead and timestamped. See drive link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1aBcdExampleDriveLink and attached dr-test-202608-replay.log. For audit purposes we can export the notarized manifest with SHA256 and a PGP signature — let us know if you need the PGP-signed bundle.

Let me know if you want the PGP bundle and we will provision it to your secure intake.

Cheers,
Priyom Das
Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
